Md Umbar Ali, Advocate ---For the Applicant. 
Mahbubey-Alam, Attorney-General with Mahfuza Begum, Assistant Attorney-General, Abdur Rahim Bhuiyan, Assistant Attorney-General--For the Respondent.
parties:
Glaxo Smith Kline Bangladesh Ltd.  ----- Applicant
vs
Commissioner of Taxes ----- Respondent
full_judgment: 11. In view of the submissions made by the learned Attorney-General and the points raised by him, this bench felt the necessity to take an expert opinion, and, as such, requested Mr MA Noor, a leading lawyer in this field, to assist this Court. Accordingly, Mr MA Noor appeared and took us through section 35 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 1984 and submits that in the instant case, the income tax authority, without taking into consideration any of the legal aspects of the case and true import of section 35 of the Income Tax Ordinance, most illegally disallowed the expenditures in the profit and loss accounts without any material basis and without arriving at a positive finding that the income, profit and gain of the assessee-applicant cannot be computed in accordance with the method of accounts employed by the assessee-applicant and, as such, disallowances made by the income tax authority in the trading expenses is beyond the scope of law. He further submits that it is only when the Revenue Authority is of the opinion that the method of accounting employed by the assessee do not reflect the true profit, income or gain of the assessee company then and only then, the department resorted to estimate upon rejecting the audited accounts expressly. In this connection, he submits that assessee-applicant is a company incorporated under the Company Act. While submitting its return, the assessee has complied with the provision of section 35(3) of the Ordinance, 1984 and a legal presumption is attached to the certificate issued by the chartered accountant and in the instant case, there is no material on record to rebut the legal presumption as to the correctness of the audited accounts of the applicant and this aspect of the case has lost sight of the Income Tax Authority. Mr MA Noor submits that there is no doubt that the taxing authority can resort to the proviso of section 35(4) but only when it finds that the method of accounting by the assessee is not regular or do not reflect the correct picture of profit, income or gain of the assessee Company. But in the instant case, there is no such finding. He further submits that the finding of the Income Tax Authority on this matter is not to be a subjective or an arbitrary decision but a judicial decision and cannot be accepted if there are no materials to support his findings. In support of his submission Mr MA Noor referred to the cases of Sagorica & Co (Pvt) Ltd vs Commissioner of Taxes 1999 BTD 87 = 52 DLR 484; Friends Corporation vs Commissioner of Taxes 1975 BTD 221 = 27 DLR 566; Commissioner of Taxes vs Friends Corporation 1978 BTD (AD) 140; Titas Gas Ltd vs Commissioner of Taxes 2000 BTD 77 = 53 DLR 209 and other cases of our jurisdiction.
